\subsection*{Expanders --- Mixing: Results}

\begin{definition}[Euclidean indicator vector]
\lean{Expander.indicator}
\statementsource{Vad12}{pdf-bf2ce5422088-p093-b003}
\label{Expander.indicator}
\leanok
For a subset $S$ of $\{0,\ldots,n-1\}$, its indicator vector in $\mathbb R^n$ has
coordinate $1$ at indices in $S$ and coordinate $0$ at all other indices.
\end{definition}

\begin{theorem}[Expander Mixing Bound for Subsets]
\lean{Expander.inner_indicator_mulVec_le}
\label{Expander.inner_indicator_mulVec_le}
\leanok
\uses{Expander.IsSymmStochastic, Expander.indicator, Expander.inner_eq_sum, Expander.inner_toCLM_right, Expander.inner_uniform_self, Expander.lambda, Expander.mulVec_uniform, Expander.norm_mulVec_le_lambda, Expander.toCLM, Expander.uniform}
\difficulty{6}
Let $n$ be a nonnegative integer and let $A$ be a symmetric real $n\times n$ matrix with
nonnegative entries and every row summing to $1$. Let $\lambda(A)$ be the supremum of
$\|Av\|$ over unit vectors orthogonal to the constant vector with every coordinate
$1/n$, and suppose $\lambda(A)\leq\lambda$. For subsets $S,T\subseteq\{1,\ldots,n\}$,
the indicator vectors satisfy
\[\left|\langle 1_S,A1_T\rangle-\frac{|S||T|}{n}\right|\leq \lambda\sqrt{|S||T|}.\]
\end{theorem}
